So how do missiles actually fly and destroy targets? I'm guessing that the Behind enemy Lines missiles that do 180's to track targets behind them don't exist. But what maneuvering can missiles do? Can they do a 180 degree turn? How much will a missile actually chase a target? Do they actually aim to hit aircraft or are they set to detonate at X metres to the target and damage with shrapnel? Are they all explosive missiles or are there variants that cause damage with shrapnel?
How do Air to Air/SAM missiles actually work?

When the missile is launched, a computer calculate the shortest distance to the target. There are some systems that track the target and sent the data back to the computer for further calculations. The missile have radars build in, so when it is near the target it doesn't depend on the truck/aircraft/warship or whatever is the main controller. The rocket fins acts against the air resistence to change the missile's direction.

How much will a missile actually chase a target?

Until it runs out of fuel or it can't track the target.

Do they actually aim to hit aircraft or are they set to detonate at X metres to the target and damage with shrapnel?

When it is at the optimum distance, the warhead detonates. Sometimes iron fragments are thrown toward the target to impair its functionality.

ELI5 version:

The missile "sees" the target through some sort of emissioin and follows it. If the missile has enough range then it can do a 180, but there are big constraints on that. When it gets close enough it explodes and shoots metal at the target. Almost all use explosives to create shrapnel, except for ones against satellites. They use a single slug (like from a gun) to hit the target.

Non ELI5 version:

Sometimes the guidance data is fed from a third party. Say a jet launches a missile, but the missile is being fed trajectory information from an AWACs radar. The F-22 never did anything beyond firing the missile. All guidance information is being uploaded

Most missiles of that type have a terminal phase detection method. This is usually a common method for tracking.

Common tracking methods are:

active: on board radar emitter and receiver so the missile does all the work. This is a fire and forget weapon.

semi - active: they have no active on board radar emitter, only a receiver. instead they use another radar source (launching aircraft / truck / ship / etc)

passive: these rely on emissions from the aircraft. this includes heat from the engines, the target's own radar for ARM, and even optical light.

I read somewhere that missiles rarely "Chase" the instead intercept. Firing a missile at a plane travelling directly towards you or away from you is generally a low percentage shot. Rather missiles "intercept" their targets from the sides.

Is that accurate?

From what I understand (I have never worked directly with SAM / A2A systems), most shots are from the rear area. The speed of missiles and the speed of aircraft make hitting them head on extremely hard. Plus the chances are very low that the target will be flying directly toward or away from you anyway.

I'm making this head on to simplify the concept, but if you have a jet going 1,400 mph and a missile going at it doing 3,500 mph that means a closure rate of almost 5,000 mph. Getting a hit at those speeds, when the tiniest course change is a huge area, is extremely difficult.

Plus, flying at a closing missile will make most countermeasure systems useless. Jamming could work, but chaff and flares are designed to mask you. If you're flying in front of the mask it kind of defeats the purpose.

For going away, it becomes an issue of range and target loss. Whether the missile can overcome the distance between the launcher and the target before it runs out of fuel. It is also means chaff and flares will be most effective as all the target has to do is drop countermeasures and keep going.

From the sides is the best as counter measures will fall behind the target and the closing rate isn't insane. But, as you said, the launcher has to fire at where it thinks the aircraft will be instead of where it is. If the aircraft maneuvers it can get out of the range the missile can maneuver to catch it.

It's a whole cat and mouse game with this and there's missile systems designed for different scenarios.

I thought it was interesting that I read somewhere that the SR-71 had over 2,500 missiles fired at it during the life of the program. During that time, not a single one hit. It relied on being so high and fast that the window to detect and successfully launch was too low for systems of the time. No one could detect it on radar, upload targeting to the missiles, and get a shot off in time to hit it even though there were missiles that had the speed and range to pull it off. I think one of the reasons it was retired was because SAM systems were getting to the point to be able to pull it off.

Hey everyone,

I'm writing this to solicit your opinion on how you think this place should operate. I have already written some very basic rules as detailed here. I do not think they require any further justification. Other than that, it is my desire to keep this place as rule-free as possible but it is quite possible that you, the users, have something in mind that I may have missed. In fact, I want your opinion on several things:

Recent Events

On another community similar to this, there is a rule regarding the posting and discussion of recent (happened <1yr ago) "active" unsolved mysteries. I imagine that rule is to prevent wild speculation and rumor spreading that may impede any ongoing investigations of a crime by law enforcement. I'm at the moment, hesitant to make that an official rule because it will hamper discussion, the subverse is quite small, and there is no indication at the moment that any discussion here is a risk or impedence to law enforcement or official investigations. What are your thoughts on this?

Quality of Posts

As I said in the rules thread, I don't want to impose anything unnecessary on the users, but there may be a point where posting of things like memes, .gifs, jokes and things of a non-serious nature start drowning out any serious discussion. My ideal solution is to let the community downvote them instead of deleting them. What exactly are your thoughts on this? Would you rather there be a moderator that monitors the subverse for this stuff and actively delete them, or would you rather have it stay up? Keep in mind that anything any moderators do, including myself, will show up in the public mod log.

I realize that having the community do it instead will depend on the culture and the type of community we have, but we are quite small at the moment, and this may require some cultivation. At the moment, this isn't a serious concern at all. None of the submissions thus far have been any of the above, but it's good to plan ahead and I want to know what you think.

Deletions & Bans

I don't want to ban anyone and if anyone breaks the rules (doxxing, witchhunting, etc.), I will give them a warning. If they do it again, I will ban them.

I also don't want to remove any comments (except for anything that violates the rules). If someone says something truly offensive (racism, sexism, things of that nature), you need to downvote them. However, if this becomes a serious re-occuring problem, and the community at large wants something done about it, I (or another mod) will take action. What do you think about this?

There's also the issue of trolling. How do we define this?

Moderators

I cannot monitor this sub all the time, so I will need help. So yes, there will be moderators in the future. I'm willing to assign mod powers to someone (or maybe several people) that agree with and adhere to my principles of moderation and aren't going to readily delete anything. For the most part, as a moderator you will do nothing at all.

Furthermore, the moderators that I want are people that are heavily invested and interested in the subject. That means they have to actually be interested in unsolved mysteries.

I also want them to be a member of good standing amongst the community and be a moderator of no more than 1 other community. This is because I don't want this subverse to be part of any moderator social group where you run into problems of cronyism and users being targeted because of whatever goes on in another subverse.

Flairs

This is something I'm going to work on over the next week or so. RIght now, my intent to create flairs for every category of unsolved mystery. What are your thoughts and suggestions here?

Anything Else

So there may be things I've left out or haven't thought of. Let me know if there's anything serious that I should address. Thanks!

From W3schools:

The <label> tag defines a label for an <input> element.

The <label> element does not render as anything special for the user. However, it provides a usability improvement for mouse users, because if the user clicks on the text within the <label> element, it toggles the control.

The for attribute of the <label> tag should be equal to the id attribute of the related element to bind them together.
